problem: Setting up and understanding server and code environments was slow; product offered instant sandboxed server environments.

founders.name: Kyle Gray
founders.background_notes: YC page says he later created sqlc.

founders.name: Brandon Liu
founders.background_notes: YC page says he works on Protomaps.

competitors.name: Koding
competitors.what: Browser-based development environment with free cloud VMs

competitors.name: Nitrous.IO
competitors.what: Cloud development environments with on-demand boxes

technical_complexity.rationale: Provisioning isolated server environments on demand needs real systems work, though built on existing virtualization at the time.

defensibility.rationale: Cloud dev environment space already had Koding and Nitrous.IO; no distinctive moat found.

market_need_then: Not independently documented; competitors launched public betas in 2012 and 2013 indicating developer interest.

branding.domain_note: stackmachine.com is now used by an unrelated company (an agent infrastructure product powered by Wasmer) per a 2026 fetch.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is a generic computer science term; web searches returned only CS pages, so search visibility was poor.

outcome_analysis: StackMachine started in May 2013 building instant sandboxed server environments, and entered a crowded space with Koding and Nitrous.IO. Nothing public explains why it went inactive, and the cause is not public. The generic computer science name gave no search visibility, which is a minor sourced observation only, so confidence is low.
notes: stackmachine.com now belongs to a different, current company, so the original site is effectively dead. No funding found. Cause of inactivity not public. brand_confusion is a weak inference from the generic name and failed search; low confidence. Nitrous.IO and Koding dates come from search snippets and URLs; the pages themselves were not opened.
